Over the years, Seventh-day Adventists have been called many things. “Cult” is one of them.

And to be honest, some people have experienced church environments that felt rigid, extreme, or even controlling. That shouldn’t be brushed aside. Church culture isn’t always healthy, and sometimes people have been hurt.

But an unhealthy culture or poor leadership doesn’t define the official beliefs of a global church. And it doesn’t reflect the character of Christ we’re called to represent.

If you’re curious about what Adventists believe, we’d rather you hear it from us directly.

I found a journal in a shoebox in my mother's attic three weeks after she died.

It was March of last year. We were cleaning out her house in Roanoke to get it ready for sale, and my brother Wade had pulled down the attic ladder and asked me to come up because there was "stuff up here that's gonna make you cry, Linda."

He wasn't wrong.
